title: An Old Reaction with New Results: The Unexpected Formation of a Rare Earth Metal Cluster Containing Six Europium Atoms

synthesis.procedure: A mixture of europium chloride hydrate (10 mmol, 3.66 g) and 4-bromobenzoylacetone 2 (30 mmol, 5.97 g) in ethanol (30 mL) was heated under reflux. Just before refluxing, triethylamine (35 mmol) was added. The mixture was heated under reflux for 30 min. The solvent was removed in vacuo, the residue was washed with water (2 × 20 mL), filtered, redissolved in 50 mL of toluene, and dried with magnesium sulphate. After 30 min the solvent was removed and the crystalline product was air-dried at room temperature, giving slightly yellow crystals of 3. Single crystals were obtained by diffusion with chloroform/n-heptane.
synthesis.time: reflux 30 min after NEt3 addition; drying 30 min after redissolution in toluene
synthesis.vessel_or_method: reflux in ethanol; single crystals by chloroform/n-heptane diffusion
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: solvent removed in vacuo; residue washed with water (2 × 20 mL), filtered, redissolved in toluene (50 mL), dried with MgSO4; solvent removed and product air-dried at rt. Single crystals by chloroform/n-heptane diffusion.

properties.summary: Typical Eu(III) luminescence from cluster 3. Overview emission spectrum in ethanol at 20 °C (λexc = 331 nm) shows 5D0 → 7FJ transitions. UV/Vis absorption at 331 nm; fluorescence quantum yield φF = 0.004 ± 0.001 and lifetime τ = 0.24 ms.
